geometry_edits.rationale: Deepen the west-facing public threshold so the access edge reads as a clearer entry seam rather than a shallow bite.
Broaden the carved opening to strengthen public void presence while keeping the dominant mass intact.
Lower the notch slightly to emphasize a grounded public cut at the access edge and improve street-level legibility.

rationale: The candidate is a coherent early-stage mass with one readable dominant figure: a compact low-rise body with an upper swell and a west-side notch that partially answers the access edge. It aligns with the neighborhood_living brief better than a generic box, and its silhouette is more resolved than a simple stair-step stack. The main weakness is that the public void is still small and somewhat implicit; the access response is present but not yet strongly legible as a true court, entry seam, or grounded threshold. Sectional/program fit is only moderate because the mass reads as a solid object more than a clearly inhabited terraced or courtyard building, but it does not violate the neighborhood typology or the access/frontage contract. The references support a stronger version of the same language: courtyard-led, bridged, terraced, and horizontally grounded rather than sculpturally isolated.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More sculptural and courtyard-led than this candidate; do not copy the roof articulation literally.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Three-part low-rise composition with a central void and a clear bridge/upper connector creates a legible public center without losing overall mass unity.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much larger and more distributed than the current compact massing.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Campus-like grouping around a shared open court can support neighborhood mixed-use when the ground plane remains public and legible.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is more transparent and planar; candidate is more compact and solid.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A strong horizontal datum with a central void and a responsive roof edge can give a low-rise mixed-use building civic presence.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The reference is more explicit in its terrace/ribbon section and circulation depth.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced, connected masses with a bridging entry and a readable public sequence are directly transferable to this neighborhood program.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This candidate is tighter and more monolithic, with less clear multi-wing separation.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Interlocking rectilinear volumes around a large courtyard can preserve hierarchy while opening the ground threshold.

warnings: Parcel containment appears satisfied in the visible views; no boundary violation is evident.
The form is coherent across views, though the public void could be deeper and more explicit.
Avoid over-correcting toward pure sculptural tiering; the program wants active ground and clear threshold logic.
